site.title: Keni | Money tracked without the friction
site.description: An open-source, self-hosted personal finance tracker. Log expenses by typing naturally, scanning receipts, or speaking. Fast local processing, multi-currency support, and zero cloud markups.

footer.tagline: Detailed financial records without the tedious bookkeeping.

hero.headline: Money tracked without the friction.
hero.sub: Type a quick sentence, snap a paper receipt, or speak out loud. Keni parses the amount, category, tags, and date into an editable staging preview so your records stay thorough in seconds.
hero.exampleLabel: Animated example: plain-language entries such as "lunch with the team 38" get labelled with amount, category, tags and date.

examples.text: uber to the airport 640 twd yesterday
2 lattes at blue bottle 11.50 for work

features.label: Features
features.title: Bookkeeping that stays out of your way.
features.sub: Granular records, multi-wallet organization, and flexible AI models, all running on your own terms.

capture.label: Capture
capture.title: Log it the way it happens.

items.title: ⌘ K to log anything
items.body: Hit ⌘K anywhere to log income, expenses, recurring bills, or multi-item splits in natural language. Keni infers the details and stages them for quick review before anything commits to your database.

items.title: Receipt & invoice scanning
items.body: Upload a photo of a paper receipt or a PDF invoice. Keni extracts the merchant, date, and individual line items into itemized records, processed in memory without storing raw files.

items.title: Voice input
items.body: Tap the mic and say what you spent. An embedded Whisper model transcribes your voice in memory on your own server, so no audio ever leaves your machine.

organize.label: Organize
organize.title: Instant recall when you need it.

items.title: Categories & tags
items.body: Context-aware tags and categories adapt to your spending habits over time. Routine transactions categorize themselves automatically, with clean filtering across your entire history.

items.title: Multiple wallets
items.body: Keep personal, freelance, shared, and travel expenses completely separate. Each wallet maintains its own native currency, exchange rates, and ledger history, built for cross-border life.

items.title: Budgets
items.body: Set monthly limits by category, wallet, or overall spend. Clear pacing bars show where you stand against your targets without loud warnings or artificial guilt.

items.title: Dashboard at a glance
items.body: A calm, uncluttered overview: monthly totals, weekly burn rate, category breakdowns, and recent activity, surfaced without decorative chrome.

items.title: Chat with your data
items.body: Ask questions in plain English: 'How much did I spend on dining out last month?' or 'What are my active recurring subscriptions?' Keni queries your actual ledger and returns exact numbers.

items.title: Bring your own AI
items.body: Plug in your own API key for Google Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI, or OpenRouter. Take advantage of generous free tiers (like Gemini Flash) or run local models with zero subscription markups.

items.title: MCP & API
items.body: With native Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, tools like Claude Desktop or Cursor can query and update your ledger directly. Use personal API tokens to automate entries from custom scripts and shortcuts.

chat.question: How did my dining spending change compared to last month?
chat.answer: You spent $496 across 14 dining entries in October, down 12% from September. Your largest single bill was $64 at Hollow Oak Bakery.

privacy.label: Open source · Self-hosted
privacy.title: Your data stays yours.
privacy.sub: Host Keni on your own server or VPS. No telemetry, no ad tracking, and no monetization of your transaction history. Just your data in your own PostgreSQL database.
checklist: PostgreSQL database hosted entirely on your server
Direct AI API calls with zero intermediary proxies
In-memory Whisper transcription so voice data never touches the cloud
Full data ownership with instant CSV and JSON export

cta.title: Detailed bookkeeping on your own terms.
cta.sub: Deploy in two minutes with Docker Compose, or try the free hosted instance to explore the workflow.

privacyPolicy.pageDescription: How Keni handles your data: what is stored, what is sent to your AI provider, how long the hosted instance keeps it, and how self-hosting differs.
privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
intro: Keni is an open-source personal finance tracker. This policy explains what data Keni collects, where it goes, and how long it is kept. It is written from the source code, so it describes what the software actually does rather than what a template says.

It covers three things: the marketing website at keni.seria.moe, the free hosted instance at app.keni.seria.moe, and the Keni software itself when you run it on your own server. When you self-host, the person running that server is responsible for the data on it, not us. The sections below say where the two cases differ.

sections.heading: Who operates Keni
body: Keni is maintained by an individual developer and published under an open-source license on GitHub. The hosted instance is run by the same maintainer as a free service so people can try Keni without setting anything up. It is not a company, and there is no sales, marketing, or advertising operation behind it.
For any question or request about your data, email seria.ati@gmail.com or open an issue on the GitHub repository.

sections.heading: Data you give Keni
body: Everything below is stored in Keni's PostgreSQL database. On the hosted instance that database is on the maintainer's server. When you self-host, it is on yours.
list: Account: a username, your password (stored only as a bcrypt hash, never in plain text), and optional profile settings such as display name, timezone, language, preferred currency, whether to use historical exchange rates, and a custom instruction for the AI.

Financial records: wallets with their name and currency, transactions with type, amount, description, date, and tags, plus categories, tags, budgets, recurring transaction rules, and links or groups between transactions.

AI provider settings: which provider you chose (Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenAI, or OpenRouter), the model names you selected, whether local OCR is enabled, and your API key. The API key is stored base64-encoded, which is an encoding and not encryption. Anyone with access to the database can read it. Use a dedicated key with a spending limit and revoke it at your provider if you stop using Keni.
API tokens: a name, an expiry date, when the token was last used, and a SHA-256 hash of the token. The raw token is shown once and is not stored.
MCP connections: for AI agents connected over MCP, the client's registered name and redirect URLs, short-lived authorization codes, and hashed access and refresh tokens with their scopes and expiry.

Uploaded files: receipt images, PDF invoices, and voice recordings are processed in memory and are not written to disk or to the database. Only the text or transaction data extracted from them is kept, as part of the transaction you save.

sections.heading: Data collected automatically
body: Keni has no analytics, no tracking pixels, no advertising identifiers, and sets no cookies. The website and the app both load fonts from Google Fonts, which means Google receives your IP address and browser details when the page loads.
list: Timezone: the app sends your browser's timezone with every request so dates are filtered in your local day. It is used for the request and not stored unless you save a timezone in your profile.

Browser storage: the app keeps your login tokens and the last wallet you opened in your browser's local storage. Exchange rates are cached in memory for up to a day. Nothing else is stored on your device.

Server logs: the web server keeps ordinary access logs (IP address, request path, time, user agent). Application logs record failures with your user ID, and when you use the chat feature they record which data tools the AI called and with what arguments, which can include the transaction details being searched, created, or changed. Logs are used for operating and debugging the service and are not used to profile you. On the hosted instance, logs are kept for one day.

sections.heading: Where your data is sent
body: Keni does not sell data, does not share it with advertisers, and does not send it anywhere for its own purposes. Data leaves the server only in the cases below, and each one is triggered by something you set up or asked for.
list: Your AI provider: Keni ships with no AI model. Nothing is sent to any AI service until you add your own API key. Once you do, the text you type, transcripts of your voice input, receipt images (or, if OCR is enabled and the text is readable, only the text extracted locally), text extracted from PDFs, your category names, tag names, wallet names and currencies, up to fifteen of your recent transaction descriptions used as style examples, your custom AI instruction, and your timezone are sent to the provider you chose. In the chat feature, your message is sent along with any transaction lists, summaries, and breakdowns the model asks for, and the model can create, update, or delete transactions on your behalf. What the provider does with that data is governed by your agreement with them, not by this policy.

Frankfurter (api.frankfurter.dev): a free exchange-rate service. Both your browser and the server ask it for rates using only currency codes and dates. No account or transaction data is included, but the request from your browser reveals your IP address to that service.

MCP clients and API integrations: when you authorize an AI agent over MCP or create a personal API token, that client can read and modify all of your Keni data through the API. You choose what to connect, and you can revoke access at any time from the app.
Google Fonts: loaded by the website and the app, as described above.

sections.heading: Voice input
body: Speech-to-text runs on the Keni server itself using a local Whisper model. Your recording is not sent to any third party for transcription, is processed in memory, and is not stored. The transcript is then handled like typed text, which means it is sent to your AI provider to extract the transaction. The configuration has an option for an external speech-to-text provider, but it is not implemented and returns an error if enabled.

sections.heading: Retention and deletion
body: On the hosted instance, your data is kept until you delete it. There is no automatic deletion.
When you self-host, your data is kept until you delete it or the server operator does. Keni includes an optional job that automatically deletes old transactions, but it is off by default.
list: You can delete transactions, wallets (which removes their transactions), categories, tags, budgets, recurring rules, API tokens, and your AI provider settings from within the app at any time.
You can export any wallet's transactions as CSV or JSON at any time.

You can delete your whole account from Settings → Data. This immediately and permanently removes your account together with all wallets, transactions, categories, tags, budgets, recurring rules, API tokens, MCP connections, and AI provider settings. It cannot be undone, so export your wallets first if you want a copy.

sections.heading: Security
body: The hosted instance is served over HTTPS. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt. API tokens and MCP tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes. Login sessions use short-lived access tokens (thirty minutes) with refresh tokens valid for thirty days. Data is not encrypted at rest beyond what the hosting disk provides, and as noted above your AI provider key is stored encoded rather than encrypted.

The hosted instance is a free service run by one person, with no uptime guarantee. Exporting your wallets now and then is a good way to keep your own copy. If you want full control over where your data lives, self-host.

sections.heading: Self-hosting
body: When you run Keni on your own server, the maintainer receives nothing from your instance. The software has no telemetry, no update checks, and no connection back to the maintainer. The only outbound connections it makes are to the AI provider you configure and to Frankfurter for exchange rates. In that setup, whoever operates the server is responsible for the data and for any policy their users need.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
body: If Keni starts collecting or sharing something new, this page will be updated and the date at the top will change. Because Keni is open source, you can also read the code on GitHub to check that this policy matches what the software does.

support.pageDescription: Need help with Keni? Reach the maintainer by email, Discord, or open an issue on GitHub.
support.title: Support
support.intro: Keni is built and maintained by one person. Pick whichever channel suits you; bug reports and feature requests are best on GitHub so others can find them.

channels.label: Email
channels.note: For account issues on the hosted instance, or anything you would rather not post publicly.

channels.label: Discord server
channels.note: Community server. Ask in the open and other users may help too.

channels.label: GitHub
channels.note: Open an issue for bugs, feature requests, and self-hosting problems.
